title: Rosenberg rehabilitation-aftercare+ (RoReNa+): Evaluation of the extended, internet-based/mobile-based Rehabilitation follow-up support platform - initially indication-specific for people with obesity or diabetes mellitus
summary:
In order to improve the sustainability of the success of rehabilitation and participation achievements, eHealth quotations open up new possibilities for follow-up achievements (e.g. aftercare services). 
A multimodal aftercare-concept is to be developed and tested for rehabilitants with obesity or diabetes mellitus. On the one hand, this concept includes the optimized or expanded post-training-/aftercare platform (“RoReNa+”); this is conceptually a knowledge portal with extensive information on the disease patterns  (obesity, diabetes mellitus). The content of the knowledge portal includes, among other things, the knowledge already acquired during the rehabilitation-measure from the training lectures as well as further information on the disease. The idea is that the rehabilitants can quickly re-read the training content they have learnt or easily research additional information in this way after the rehabilitation measure. The website also contains various self-monitoring tools.
The aftercare concept also includes the offer of personal psychological support. The entire concept is being evaluated in the context of a randomized, controlled study.

Interventions group

Control group 
Rehabilitation-Programme

Access to RoReNa+-platform for 3 months (without self-monitoring tools or  message functions), no personal support

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
main diagnosis obesity or diabetes mellitus 
signed declaration of consent to participate in the study 
technical and cognitive prerequisites for using the Internet
sufficient knowledge of the German language (especially in writing)
Exclusion criteria:
serious psychiatric illness (e.g. suicidal rehabilitants, severe eating disorder, traumatization),
serious somatic illness (carcinoma, state after LTX) that has a greater impact on the rehabilitee's prognosis than the underlying illness,
condition after bariatric surgery (aftercare is usually provided by a surgical center),
rehabilitants who do not have sufficient knowledge of the German language (especially in writing).
